lesson_title: Three Pours Exactly: Spheres, Pyramids and Cones
hook_text: Fill a cone with water. Pour it into the matching cylinder. It takes EXACTLY three pours. Always.
clip_script: Neither is a stack of identical layers, so base times height overestimates them: the layers shrink as they climb. The correction is beautiful and exact: a pyramid or cone fills exactly one third of the prism or cylinder that shares its base and height. Volume equals one third times base area times perpendicular height. That one third is a real, testable fact: take a hollow cone and a hollow cylinder with matching base and height, fill the cone with water, and pour. Three pours fill the cylinder — always, precisely, three.
visual_style: A transparent cone repeatedly filling with bright liquid and emptying into a matching cylinder, the level rising in exact thirds, with a counter ticking one, two, three as it hits the brim.
pacing: Steady pour rhythm building anticipation, snap payoff as the third pour lands exactly on the rim.
